output_json.patch_notes: Root-cause fix in AbstractResource.forFile(String relativePath): the segment-splitting regex now normalizes both '/' and '\' (`relativePath.split("[/\\\\]+")`) before the existing "." / ".." term-popping and root-boundary-check logic runs. This is the single shared normalization routine ('final' method) used by every Resource subclass (ContextResource, ClasspathResource, etc.) and every downstream asset/resource dispatcher (ContextAssetRequestHandler and any other AssetRequestHandler that forwards request-derived paths into forFile()), so the fix covers all call sites named in the alert's trace plus sibling callers, not only the POV's specific path. No behavior change for legitimate '/'-only paths; '\'-containing paths that previously survived as opaque literal terms now get properly decomposed and, if they attempt to escape the resource root, correctly throw the pre-existing IllegalStateException("...would go above root") — the same exception forward-slash traversal attempts already triggered. Added regression tests in tapestry-ioc's ClasspathResourceSpec.groovy (Spock) exercising forFile() directly with backslash, doubled-backslash, and mixed-separator traversal payloads (all expected to throw) plus a legitimate backslash-separated relative reference (expected to resolve normally, proving no functional regression).
output_json.risk_notes: Low risk: the change only affects how forFile() splits its input into segments (now recognizing '\' as an additional separator alongside '/'); the existing "." / ".." handling, empty-term skipping, and root-boundary exception logic are untouched. On Unix-style deployments this only matters for callers that pass backslash-containing paths (previously treated as a single opaque filename component); after the fix such paths are decomposed as path segments, which is the correct, security-required behavior per the alert (CWE-022, Windows-style separators are explicitly called out as security-relevant). No dependency, API, or build-system changes. ContextResourceTest and the broader tapestry-ioc/tapestry-core test suites should be run to confirm no legitimate resource-lookup path relies on backslashes being treated as literal filename characters (none were found in the existing test suite, and ClasspathResourceSpec's pre-existing tests all still pass).
output_json.summary: Fixed CWE-022 path traversal at the shared root cause: AbstractResource.forFile() (tapestry-ioc) only split relativePath on '/', so a '\'-delimited ".." segment (e.g. Windows-style paths) was never decomposed and popped by the ".." root-boundary check, letting it survive as an opaque literal term all the way to filesystem resolution (ContextResource -> ContextImpl.getRealFile / new File). Since forFile() is `final` and inherited by every Resource subclass (ContextResource, ClasspathResource, etc.), and is the sole normalization point on the ContextAssetRequestHandler -> ChecksumPath -> AbstractResource.forFile -> ContextResource -> ContextImpl trace in the alert, patching this one function closes the vulnerability for all callers/subclasses, not just the ContextAssetRequestHandler path. Changed the segment split from `relativePath.split("/")` to `relativePath.split("[/\\\\]+")` so backslashes are treated identically to forward slashes before the existing ".." popping/root-check logic runs, making both encodings provably equivalent from the caller's perspective (matches the finder's regression_hint exactly). Added Spock regression tests in ClasspathResourceSpec.groovy (which exercises the shared AbstractResource.forFile code path) covering: pure backslash traversal, doubled/run-of-backslashes, mixed '/' and '\' separators split across boundaries, and a legitimate '\'-separated relative reference that must still resolve correctly (non-regression). Verified by temporarily reverting the source fix: both new tests fail against the vulnerable code (WrongExceptionThrownError / NPE) and pass once the fix is restored; full ClasspathResourceSpec suite (27 tests) passes with the fix in place.
